daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The Anti-Corruption Commission (KPK) is supporting deliberations on the Asset Forfeiture Bill between the government and parliament, with the proposed legislation targeting passage by December 2026 and featuring five critical issues. President Prabowo defended his cabinet size, complaining that critics call it fat and inefficient, while noting Timor Leste has 28 ministers despite being a small country. Meanwhile, the KPK launched an investigation into smartboard procurement at Bogor Regency's education office.

  • The National Police chief reshuffled strategic positions at headquarters and regional commands, including appointing Brig. Gen. Hengki Haryadi as Papua Barat Daya police chief, who previously captured notorious drug suspect Hercules.
  • Gus Kikin's election as PBNU chairman brings hopes he will lead NU toward greater unity and independence, with reconciliation seen as his primary task following a contentious muktamar.
  • Police have increased the number of suspects to 49 in connection with the August 27 demonstration riots at the DPR building.
  • The army chief General Maruli Simanjuntak said that traditional tattoos are acceptable for TNI recruitment, while a Commission I leader claimed special recruitment privileges for Dayak people are not related to the forest fire crisis.
  • Several ministries and agencies have requested additional budget allocations for various programmes.
  • The Constitutional Court's ruling on national disaster status is expected to expedite assistance and recovery aspects, with the government urged to immediately follow the ruling.
  • A Poltracking Indonesia survey found that public satisfaction with Prabowo-Gibran stands at 55.1%, while freedom of expression and press freedom were rated positively.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia's Foreign Ministry is investigating claims by Ukrainian intelligence that eight Indonesian citizens were recruited by the Russian military, with DPR Commission I highlighting the high salary offers used to lure them. A DPR member warned that Indonesian citizenship status could be lost if the allegations are confirmed. The case has raised concerns about recruitment tactics targeting Indonesian workers abroad.

  • Indonesian Health Minister Budi Gunadi has entered the race to become the next World Health Organization chief.
  • Indonesia and South Korea are jointly investigating an alleged human trafficking ring on Jeju Island involving Indonesian nationals, with the Foreign Ministry coordinating with South Korean authorities.
  • Indonesia-Japan defense cooperation has expanded to include forest fire response capabilities.
  • Indonesia has renewed its bid for the ICAO Council after a 25-year absence.
  • The Foreign Ministry confirmed that all Indonesian citizens in Nepal are safe following the recent disaster.

Other

Pertamina has increased fuel prices, with the new price list taking effect September 1, 2026. Pertamina cited specific considerations for adjusting Pertamax Turbo prices. The fuel price adjustment comes as multiple sectors face inflationary pressures, with the government working to balance subsidies and market conditions.

  • The government's free meal program for pregnant women and toddlers has reached 10.8 million recipients nationwide.
  • Environmental authorities have investigated 19 companies linked to forest fires burning 11,000 hectares in Kalimantan and Sumatra, with the Ministry of Environment sealing 19 business entities, while Indonesia has deployed 53 aircraft to fight fires.
  • The Transbandara bus fare from Blok M to Soekarno-Hatta Airport has increased to Rp 15,000 starting today.
  • State holding company Danantara has disbursed Rp 456 billion to rescue the stalled LRT City project.
  • Indonesia has facilitated the first export of Tangkuban Parahu Arabica coffee to Saudi Arabia, while the government targets oil lifting of 612,500 bpd in 2027 and has set eight industrial priorities for next year.
